text:
aria: Quick follow-up on safetensors handoff + eager hotstart compatibility. Ran a canary and hit OOMs when loader attempted hotstart on a bundle with mixed safetensors and gz shards. Short dump: loader expects contiguous offsets but compressed shards alter mmap layout -> eviction thrash.

josh: Can you paste the minimal log + repro steps?

aria: Logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-18T15:02:31Z WARN warmup: hotstart failed: mmap read beyond shard bounds
stack: warmup.hotstart -> loader.map_shard -> mmap_fault
model: mosaic-1.0 sharded(32) mixed-format
```
Repro: curl the canary bundle + run `pytest tests/warmup/test_hotstart.py::test_mixed_shard_hotstart --eager-warmup`. CI run hangs then OOMs.

kai: Looks like the handoff tuple between weights-sourcer and loader ({shard_id, size, url, checksum}) is underspecified for mmap/hotstart which needs per-chunk on-disk layout or offsets.

maria: We need a backward-compatible approach. My proposal: extend the model manifest with an optional `hotstart_layout` map per shard (e.g., list of chunk offsets/sizes and compression flags) and bump the manifest version. New loaders consume it; old loaders ignore the field.

josh: Less invasive alternative: add a runtime probe shim in the loader that reads a small head/tail of each shard to detect format (safetensors header vs gzip magic vs a custom packer). This requires no manifest change but has per-shard latency cost and depends on range support.

aria: Measured probe cost: ~0.15-0.3ms/shard on local disk, ~5-20ms/shard for remote S3 (depends on range latency). Warmup tends to be latency sensitive so probes can add up across many shards. Also note some CDNs/proxies don't honor range requests reliably.

kai: Trade-offs summary: manifest metadata = one-time, precise, no probing overhead; shim/probe = zero-manifest-change but runtime overhead and brittle on stores without range. I think we should do manifest-first with a probe fallback.

maria: Rollout plan (sketch):
1) Add optional `hotstart_layout` in manifest (no enforcement).
2) Implement loader to consume layout if present.
3) Add probe shim behind feature flag `EAGER_HOTSTART_PROBE=true` for clusters that need it.
4) Canary rollout and monitor.

deploy-bot: Canary created: eng-ml-canary -> 10% hosts for 1h, then 50% for 6h if OK. PR will be annotated with canary tag.

ops-bot: Please add metrics: `warmup_failure_count`, `warmup_probe_latency_ms_p50_p95`, `hotstart_success_rate`. Alert if `warmup_failure_count > 5` in 1h.

aria: Pseudo-code for the probe shim I sketched:
```
function detect_shard_format(url, shard_id, manifest=None):
  if manifest and manifest.hotstart_layout and shard_id in manifest.hotstart_layout:
    return manifest.hotstart_layout[shard_id]  # explicit layout wins
  head = http_range_get(url, bytes=0-128)  # small probe, cacheable
  if head.startswith(b"safetensors") or b"safetensors" in head:
    return 'safetensors'
  if head.startswith(b"\x1f\x8b"):
    return 'gzip'
  return 'unknown'
```
Notes: probes require presigned URL reuse for efficiency and a fallback path when range isn't supported. Also need to handle truncated heads.

josh: Edge cases to add to test matrix: signed URL expiry during probe, range-not-supported (HTTP 200 full-body), presign reuse, truncated head, and S3 slow-range scenarios. Add unit tests for partial reads and a simulated S3 backend for benchmarks.

maria: Action items: aria -> PR for manifest schema + example bundles; kai -> prototype loader shim + microbench; josh -> test harness + S3 sim benchmarks; ops -> add canary metrics & alerts. Release note copy: "loader: supports optional `hotstart_layout` in model manifest for eager hotstart; loader falls back to probe-based detection when enabled via feature flag."

aria: I'll open the PR today and tag @eng-ml for review. Will include compatibility tests and the canary plan. :thumbsup:

maria: Prefer manifest-first approach. Thanks all. :eyes:
